acme:
# Example company pack. Fictional company: copy and adapt.
# Keep your own pack in your product repository (for example .hdsf/packs/acme.yaml) and list it in hdsf.yaml:
#   packs: [.hdsf/packs/acme.yaml]

pack:
  id: acme
  title: ACME Health data policy
  jurisdiction: ORG
  version: "1.0.0"
  date: 2026-11-23
  maintainer: "ACME Health, privacy and clinical safety team"
  status: "In force for all ACME Health products"
  url: null

policy:
  minimum_level: 2
  no_go: [CORE-TRK-01, CORE-TRK-03, CORE-AI-03, CORE-DAT-10]
  forbid_dependencies: ["@hotjar/browser", logrocket, "@fullstory/browser"]
  forbid_phrases: ["last chance", "only today", "don't lose your streak", "você", "não percas a tua sequência"]
  require_decision_for_features: [ai_generative, ai_clinical, research_use]
  review_every_days: 180

rules:
  - id: ACME-CLN-01
    title: A clinician signs off every health content change
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    users: [all]
    requirement: Any change to health information, thresholds or safety messages is reviewed and signed by a named ACME clinician before release.
    rationale: ACME decision after an internal incident review; supports CORE-SAF-02.
    improvement: Add a clinical sign-off step to the release checklist and record it in the content register.
    effort: low
    sources: [ACME-POLICY, ISO-82304-2]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: ACME-DES-01
    title: Personal risk scores come with a plain explanation
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    users: [all]
    requirement: A personal risk score is never shown alone. It comes with a natural frequency ("about 3 in 100 people like you"), an icon array and what the person can do next.
    rationale: ACME decision based on research on risk communication (Galesic 2009).
    improvement: Use the ACME risk card component for every score.
    effort: medium
    sources: [ACME-POLICY, R-GALESIC2009]
    detection:
      method: manual
portugal:
# hdsf.yaml template for a product used in Portugal. The Portugal pack (packs/pt.yaml) loads by itself because
# countries lists PT: digital consent age 13, CNPD, INFARMED, CEIC, CNCS, 112 and SNS 24, texts in Portuguese.
hdsf_version: "0.2"

product:
  name: "Nome do produto"
  version: 0.1.0
  url: https://example.pt
  maker: "Empresa, Lda."
  contact: privacidade@example.pt

intended_purpose: >
  Write one or two full sentences: what the product is for, for whom and what it claims.

profiles: [core]
users: [public]
features: [accounts]
countries: [PT]
packs: []                    # company or sector packs, for example .hdsf/packs/acme.yaml

qualification:
  medical_device: undecided  # none | mdsw | ivd | annex_xvi
  class: null
  notified_body: null
  rationale: docs/qualificacao.md

data:
  gdpr_role: controller
  records: docs/registo-de-atividades.md
  dpia: docs/aipd.md         # AIPD: avaliação de impacto sobre a proteção de dados
  retention: null
  purposes: []               # [{name, basis, art9}]
  rights: {access: null, export: null, delete: null}
  storage_regions: [eu-south-2]
  third_parties: []          # [{name, purpose, jurisdiction, receives_health_data, dpa}]
  tracking_on_health_screens: false
  ads: none

security:
  policy: SECURITY.md
  incident_plan: docs/plano-de-incidentes.md
  sbom: null

safety:
  emergency_route: "112 e SNS 24 (808 24 24 24), a um toque, em todos os ecrãs de saúde"
  content_review: null

ehds: {ehr_system: false, claims_ehr_interoperability: false}
nis2: {status: not_in_scope}  # care providers: check Decreto-Lei n.º 125/2025 and register with the CNCS
review: {last_reviewed: null}
decisions: {}                # {feature: path to decision record}, when a company pack asks for them
waivers: []
